note: Hand-written. Members are fnmatch patterns on registry ids (source/name). 'tools' lists non-skill programs that belong to the same decision. Policies: compose = use each member for its own phase or layer; prefer-by-context = use exactly one, chosen from project signals; owner-pin = off unless the owner turns it on.

clusters.topic: Test-driven development
clusters.guidance: All teach red-green-refactor. Use the one the project already follows and never run two in the same task. With no preference, pick the one with the strictest 'verify before claiming done' wording.

clusters.topic: From idea to plan
clusters.guidance: These are phases of one flow, not rivals: explore, then spec, then plan, then tickets. Run one skill per phase. The gate scales with the task: more than 3 files needs a written plan; a small change needs a one-paragraph confirmation.

clusters.topic: Asking the user before building
clusters.guidance: All interview the user before work starts. Use one. Ask only questions whose answers change the work, prefer multiple choice, and stop asking when the remaining unknowns do not change the plan.

clusters.topic: Finding the cause of a bug
clusters.guidance: Pick one. Whatever the choice, reproduce first, find the root cause before editing, and add a regression test.

clusters.topic: Reviewing a change
clusters.guidance: Review before merge in a fresh context that did not write the change. Security-sensitive code also needs a dedicated security review; a general review does not replace it.

clusters.topic: Minimal code versus full process
clusters.guidance: Minimalist skills decide how much code to write; process skills decide how to verify it. Never cut validation, error handling, security or tests to satisfy a minimalist skill. When they pull apart, the owner's written rules break the tie.

clusters.topic: Saving context and output tokens
clusters.guidance: Different layers: caveman shortens chat prose, ponytail limits how much code is written, rtk filters shell output, context-mode sandboxes large non-shell data. Do not run two tools that rewrite the same tool's output (rtk and context-mode on Bash); pick one per matcher. Run `doctor` to detect hook collisions.

clusters.topic: Querying a codebase structurally
clusters.guidance: Structural questions about source code: codebase-memory-mcp. Mixed material (docs, PDFs, images, video): graphify. Do not index the same repository with both in one session.

clusters.topic: Reading or acting on websites and desktop apps
clusters.guidance: Reading public pages: a headless fetcher, or Scrapling when the page needs many fetches, JavaScript rendering or structured extraction to markdown. Interactive or logged-in work: the platform's browser tool, then a browser-automation skill. Debugging a page you own: chrome-devtools. Native desktop apps: computer use or agent-desktop. Repeated calls to one site you are allowed to automate: a saved API operation. Multi-source research: a research skill. Use one tool per task. Evading bot detection (stealth fingerprints, challenge solving, proxy rotation to dodge blocks) is prohibited: stay on pages the owner may read, respect robots.txt and rate limits, and stop when a site refuses automated access.

clusters.topic: Terse chat versus polished text
clusters.guidance: Chat replies may be terse. Anything that leaves the conversation (documents, commits, messages to other people, published copy) is written in normal prose. Never apply a compression style to outbound text.

clusters.topic: Testing a business idea or its pricing
clusters.guidance: Before launch: the founder-* skills. Pricing of a product already in the market: pricing. Named competitors with dated sources: a market-check step that cites sources. Do not present model opinion as market data.

clusters.topic: Analyzing software or sites you did not write
clusters.guidance: Dual use. Only for software or sites you own or are authorized in writing to analyze. Off unless the user names the target and confirms authorization in the conversation.

clusters.topic: Keeping durable memory for agents across sessions
clusters.guidance: Pick one durable store per project and write to it only. PARA files suit personal or project notes, the elephant-goldfish model suits per-folder README context for a repository, the wiki skills suit a curated document wiki. Never store secrets or personal data of third parties in memory. Check what the platform memory already holds before adding a second store.

clusters.topic: Speech to text and text to speech
clusters.guidance: Direction decides: audio in, transcript out uses a speech-to-text tool; text in, audio out uses a text-to-speech tool. Prefer local, offline tools for private audio so recordings do not leave the machine. Check each tool's license before commercial use, since some voice weights are non-commercial. Cloning a real person's voice needs that person's consent; never use a cloned voice for calls, impersonation or messages sent as someone else.

clusters.topic: Drafting, scheduling and posting on social networks
clusters.guidance: Drafting and planning are free; publishing is not. Nothing is posted, scheduled, replied to, commented on or sent as a direct message until the owner has seen the exact final text and said yes in the conversation. One approval covers one item. Pair the drafting skill with an approval step, and never connect a scheduler or account credentials without the owner turning it on.

clusters.topic: Avoiding generic AI output in prose, design and code
clusters.guidance: Different phases: the anti-slop rules constrain a draft while it is being produced (copy, UI, layout, code), the humanizer rewrites finished prose that still reads machine-made. Use the variant that matches the artifact (copywriting, ui, code, layout) and finish with the humanizer on outbound text. Do not apply either to chat replies, and never let a style rule change facts, numbers or claims.

clusters.topic: Marketing, copy, SEO and growth skills
clusters.guidance: The marketingskills pack shares four names with the installed copies (cold-email, copywriting, pricing, sales-enablement): use the installed claude-user copy for those and the pack for everything else. Use one skill per task, brief it with the product, audience and constraints, and run outbound text through the humanizer before it leaves the conversation.

clusters.topic: Approving drafts and outbound messages before they leave
clusters.guidance: Anything that reaches another person or system on the owner's behalf (email, chat, post, filing, order) is a draft until the owner approves that exact text. Optionally verify the draft first with two independent reviewers (santa-method), then show it with its destination and wait for an explicit yes; edits void the approval. Keep one policy per channel about who may speak and what stays silent. Off unless the owner turns it on, and then it only adds gates, never removes them.

clusters.topic: Securing agents, tools and MCP servers
clusters.guidance: Layers, not rivals: review each MCP server and dependency before registering it, harden the agent's permissions and secrets handling, review application code for vulnerabilities, and audit the running system last. A general review does not replace a dedicated security review. Registering an MCP server or changing permissions is an owner step.

clusters.topic: Market analysis and trading tools
tools: broker account or API (owner credentials, owner-run)
clusters.guidance: Analysis, scanning and paper trading only. The agent never places, confirms or routes a real order and gives no personalized investment advice; the owner executes any trade. Off unless the owner turns it on for the session.
